prompt: A machine is fast in the morning and unusable by mid-afternoon. What is that?

choices.text: a disk that is failing under a full day of use
choices.why: A disk is slow on particular files, not by the hour.

choices.text: a memory fault that shows up under a long session
choices.why: Memory corrupts and crashes; it does not slow down.

choices.text: a program that leaks and needs restarting daily
choices.why: A real thing, and then closing it would fix it.

choices.text: overheating, and the processor slowing itself down
choices.why: Fine when cold, slow when warm, and no message.

prompt: Why is thermal throttling so hard to recognise?

choices.text: it produces a slow machine and reports nothing
choices.why: No message, no error, and it is filed under software.

choices.text: it only happens on machines that are several years old
choices.why: A blocked vent does it on a new one.

choices.text: it looks exactly like a disk beginning to fail
choices.why: A disk has its own signature and a noise.

choices.text: the temperature cannot be read without special tools
choices.why: Every system reports it.

prompt: What does a machine do when it gets hotter still?

choices.text: it cuts the power instantly, with no shutdown
choices.why: The last protection there is.

choices.text: it refuses to start any new program
choices.why: Nothing does that.

choices.text: it shows a warning and closes the open programs
choices.why: There is no time for that.

choices.text: it switches the fan up to the highest setting it has
choices.why: That happened long before.

prompt: Why does a fan at full speed not fix a dusty heatsink?

choices.text: the dust makes the fan spin more slowly
choices.why: It is spinning at full speed.

choices.text: dust between the fins stops air passing at all
choices.why: The air moves and goes nowhere.

choices.text: the fan is the part that has actually failed here
choices.why: The fan is doing what it can.

choices.text: a fan at full speed produces heat of its own
choices.why: Negligible next to the processor.

prompt: Which of these help a hot laptop without opening it?

choices.text: lifting the back so air reaches the underside
choices.why: The intake is on the bottom.

choices.text: running fewer programs at the same time
choices.why: It lowers the load and leaves the cooling broken.

choices.text: keeping it off beds and sofas
choices.why: Fabric presses straight into the intake.

choices.text: blowing the loose dust out of the vents
choices.why: Worth doing, and it leaves the packed dust.

prompt: Which noise from a machine is the urgent one?

choices.text: a fan that changes pitch as the load changes
choices.why: A fan doing its job.

choices.text: a hum that gets louder when the lid is closed
choices.why: Airflow changing, and not a fault.

choices.text: a fan that rattles or buzzes continuously
choices.why: A bearing going. Cheap, and not urgent.

choices.text: a rhythmic click from a spinning hard disk
choices.why: That is the head retrying, and it is the next section.

prompt: A processor that is too hot protects itself by ___ down.
What is the first thing to do about a disk you suspect?

choices.text: copy the files off, before any test at all
choices.why: Every test spends reads that may be the last ones.

choices.text: check the warranty and arrange a replacement
choices.why: Do it after, when the data is safe.

choices.text: restart and see whether the symptom returns
choices.why: It will, and the copy is still not made.

choices.text: run a full surface test to confirm the fault
choices.why: That is an afternoon of reads it may not have.

prompt: What does SMART passing tell you?

choices.text: nothing; a share of disks fail with it reporting fine
choices.why: It is evidence in one direction only.

choices.text: that any symptoms are software rather than hardware
choices.why: It does not rule hardware out.

choices.text: that the fault is in the cable rather than the disk
choices.why: A separate test entirely.

choices.text: that the disk has years of healthy life left in it
choices.why: It says no such thing.

prompt: How does a solid-state disk differ in how it fails?

choices.text: it cannot really fail, having no moving parts at all
choices.why: It fails; the parts that wear are not mechanical.

choices.text: it fails suddenly, and it makes no noise at all
choices.why: Often going read-only or vanishing between starts.

choices.text: it slows down steadily over its whole life
choices.why: Not the pattern.

choices.text: it gives more warning than a spinning disk ever does
choices.why: Usually less.

prompt: The machine freezes for five seconds, repeatedly, and is otherwise fine. What is that?

choices.text: a memory fault reading a bad location
choices.why: That crashes rather than pauses.

choices.text: the machine waiting for a read the disk is retrying
choices.why: A pause, and then normal.

choices.text: a processor slowing itself right down because of heat
choices.why: Heat is steady slowness, not a pause.

choices.text: a network request that is timing out quietly
choices.why: Possible, and it is not a whole-machine freeze.

prompt: Why is a disk that has started failing replaced rather than repaired?

choices.text: a repair would erase everything already on it
choices.why: The copy was made first anyway.

choices.text: the repair costs more than a new disk does
choices.why: There is no repair to price.

choices.text: marking the bad sectors buys time, not health
choices.why: The mechanism that produced them is still there.

choices.text: a repaired disk cannot be read by any other machine
choices.why: It can.

prompt: Match each symptom to the part it belongs to.

pairs.left: slow only after twenty minutes of use
one file takes thirty seconds, every time
a different program crashes each day
it restarts whenever a game starts

prompt: A disk that reallocates more sectors every month is running out of ___ places to write.
What is the signature of a memory fault?

choices.text: the same program crashes at the same step
choices.why: That is a software bug, and it is reproducible.

choices.text: the machine slows down as the day goes along
choices.why: That is heat.

choices.text: the crashes move between unrelated programs
choices.why: A software bug is reproducible; this wanders.

choices.text: one file will not open and all the others will
choices.why: That is the disk.

prompt: An installation fails at a different point every time. What does the lesson say?

choices.text: the disk is too full for the installation to finish
choices.why: That fails at the same place, with a message.

choices.text: the installation media is damaged and needs remaking
choices.why: Then it would fail at the same point.

choices.text: treat it as memory until something proves otherwise
choices.why: Installing reads and writes an enormous amount.

choices.text: the download was corrupted and must be repeated
choices.why: Again, the same point each time.

prompt: What makes a memory test unusual among the tests in this course?

choices.text: it can be run while the system is being used
choices.why: It runs before the system starts.

choices.text: it takes only a few minutes to complete
choices.why: It takes hours, and it wants them.

choices.text: it repairs the faults that it happens to find
choices.why: It finds them; it repairs nothing.

choices.text: it gives an answer that is not open to interpretation
choices.why: It writes patterns and reads them back.

prompt: Why run a memory test for more than one pass?

choices.text: each pass tests a different half of the memory
choices.why: Every pass covers all of it.

choices.text: the borderline faults only appear after several
choices.why: One pass finds the worst ones.

choices.text: a single pass can report a fault that is not there
choices.why: False alarms are not the concern.

choices.text: the memory needs to warm up before it fails
choices.why: Not the reason given.

prompt: A memory test fails. What is the next step?

choices.text: replace both modules, since one has failed
choices.why: Two tests find out which, and cost nothing.

choices.text: remove one module and run on the other
choices.why: The fault follows the faulty module.

choices.text: run the test again to be sure of the result
choices.why: A failure is already unambiguous.

choices.text: reinstall the system to clear the bad locations
choices.why: Software cannot move a bad chip.

prompt: How is running out of memory different from a memory fault?

choices.text: it produces crashes in completely unrelated programs
choices.why: That is the fault.

choices.text: it gets worse as the machine warms up
choices.why: That is heat, not memory.

choices.text: it is entirely predictable, and it corrupts nothing
choices.why: Many things open, slow; closed, fine.

choices.text: it shows up in a memory test as an error
choices.why: A test on an idle machine finds nothing.

prompt: When memory runs out, the system starts using the ___ as an overflow.
Why do power faults produce symptoms all over the machine?

choices.text: the system reports a power fault as some other kind of error
choices.why: It usually reports nothing at all.

choices.text: every subsystem depends on the thing that is failing
choices.why: So the symptom is whatever happened to be running.

choices.text: the supply sends the wrong signals to each part
choices.why: It delivers power, not signals.

choices.text: a failing supply overheats the parts around it
choices.why: Not the mechanism described.

prompt: A desktop restarts during a game and never while reading mail. What is the suspect?

choices.text: the graphics card, which the game is leaning on hardest
choices.why: Possible, and the pattern points at supply first.

choices.text: the power supply, under the load the game asks for
choices.why: It restarts under load and only under load.

choices.text: the disk, which the game is reading from continuously
choices.why: A disk pauses; it does not restart the machine.

choices.text: the memory, which the game fills completely
choices.why: Memory crashes without a pattern like this.

prompt: A laptop charges only when the cable is held at an angle. What is that?

choices.text: a battery that has reached the end of its life
choices.why: A dead battery does not care about angles.

choices.text: a mechanical fault, in the socket or the plug
choices.why: Held-at-an-angle is always physical.

choices.text: a charger that is underpowered for the machine
choices.why: That would fail at every angle.

choices.text: a setting that limits charging above a threshold
choices.why: Settings do not depend on cables.

prompt: A three-year-old laptop holds two hours of charge. What is it?

choices.text: a sign that the charger is delivering too little
choices.why: That would show while plugged in.

choices.text: a battery that has failed and needs replacing today
choices.why: It is worn rather than faulty.

choices.text: a symptom of the machine running too hot
choices.why: Heat shortens life, and this is ordinary wear.

choices.text: a normal three-year-old laptop, not a fault
choices.why: Four or five hundred cycles and it holds a fraction.

prompt: Which of these are signs of a swollen battery?

choices.text: a case that no longer closes flat
choices.why: The pouch has grown inside it.

choices.text: a laptop that rocks when it sits on a table
choices.why: The underside is no longer flat.

choices.text: a battery that runs down faster than it used to
choices.why: That is ordinary wear.

choices.text: a trackpad that has risen and will not click
choices.why: The commonest first sign; the cell is right beneath it.

prompt: What must not be done to a swollen battery?

choices.text: taken to somebody who handles them for a living
choices.why: That is exactly what should happen.

choices.text: taken to a proper disposal point rather than a bin
choices.why: The correct ending.

choices.text: disconnected from the charger immediately
choices.why: Also exactly right.

choices.text: pressed on, or forced out of its compartment
choices.why: Puncturing a swollen cell is how it catches fire.

prompt: What does a torch shone at a black screen tell you?

choices.text: whether the machine has started at all
choices.why: Sound and lights answer that.

choices.text: whether the screen cable has come loose in the hinge
choices.why: That shows as lines, when the lid moves.

choices.text: whether the graphics side of the machine is alive
choices.why: A second monitor answers that.

choices.text: whether the panel works and only the backlight failed
choices.why: A faint image is there, and that is a cheaper repair.

prompt: Lines across a laptop picture that change when the lid moves. What is it?

choices.text: a driver that is confused about the resolution
choices.why: Software does not depend on an angle.

choices.text: the panel itself, which is cracked internally
choices.why: A crack does not respond to the hinge.

choices.text: the ribbon cable running through the hinge
choices.why: Extremely common, and it gets worse.

choices.text: the graphics chip overheating as it warms up
choices.why: Heat does not care about the lid.

prompt: Several keys near each other stop working. What is the usual cause?

choices.text: a driver that has stopped handling that region
choices.why: No driver works by region of the keyboard.

choices.text: the layout setting having changed to another country
choices.why: That gives wrong characters, not dead keys.

choices.text: each of those keys wearing out at the same time
choices.why: They do not fail in neighbourhoods by chance.

choices.text: a spill, even one that dried weeks ago
choices.why: The damage is under the keys and it stays.

prompt: Why plug a USB keyboard into a laptop with dead keys?

choices.text: it proves the fault is a spill rather than wear
choices.why: It says which device, not which cause.

choices.text: it resets the built-in keyboard when it is connected
choices.why: It does not reset anything.

choices.text: it separates the keyboard from the machine, for nothing
choices.why: And it makes the laptop usable meanwhile.

choices.text: it updates the driver the built-in keyboard uses
choices.why: They are separate devices.

prompt: A port that works only when the cable is held. What is true of it?

choices.text: it always gets worse and it never gets better
choices.why: And forcing a cable turns a board repair into a board.

choices.text: it will settle down once the contacts clean themselves
choices.why: Nothing cleans itself in there.

choices.text: it is a driver fault that a reinstall would fix
choices.why: Software does not depend on an angle.

choices.text: it is harmless as long as the cable is left alone
choices.why: Leaving it alone is not what happens.

prompt: What is the most reliable test in this section?

choices.text: if it happens on a second machine, it is physical
choices.why: That is the swap, and it says which device.

choices.text: if it happens after twenty minutes, it is physical
choices.why: That is heat, which is a different signature.

choices.text: if it changes when you move it, it is physical
choices.why: No software fault depends on the angle of a cable.

choices.text: if it happens in more than one program, it is physical
choices.why: That is memory, and it is a different test.

prompt: Which of these mean stop immediately?

choices.text: a swollen battery
choices.why: A safety matter, and not a computer problem.

choices.text: a fan that has started to rattle
choices.why: Annoying, cheap and not urgent.

choices.text: a burning smell from a power supply
choices.why: Unplug it at the wall.

choices.text: a hard disk that has begun to click
choices.why: Every minute spends reads that may be the last.

prompt: Something has been spilled into a machine. What is the worst thing to do?

choices.text: leave it upside down for several days
choices.why: Also right, and boring, and it works.

choices.text: switch it on to see whether it still works
choices.why: Most of the damage is done by powering it up again.

choices.text: take it to somebody who can open and clean it
choices.why: The best ending available.

choices.text: turn it off and take the battery out
choices.why: Exactly right.

prompt: Why does the lesson say to stop when you are annoyed?

choices.text: because a repair should never take more than an hour
choices.why: Many take longer and go fine.

choices.text: because the fault usually resolves itself overnight
choices.why: It does not.

choices.text: because force breaks clips and cables, not patience
choices.why: Every torn ribbon cable had somebody tired behind it.

choices.text: because tiredness makes the symptoms harder to read
choices.why: True, and not the argument made.

prompt: What decides whether a repair is a home job?

choices.text: whether a tool has to be bought to do it
choices.why: Sometimes relevant, and not the line.

choices.text: whether the part is expensive to buy on its own
choices.why: Price is a separate question.

choices.text: whether the machine is still under its warranty
choices.why: A commercial line rather than a practical one.

choices.text: whether a mistake costs the part or the machine
choices.why: A memory clip costs the module; a lid cable costs the lid.

prompt: A clicking disk is no longer found at all. What is the decision?

choices.text: whether the data is worth a recovery service
choices.why: Which anything else tried first makes less likely to work.

choices.text: which utility to run to bring the disk back
choices.why: Running utilities is what spends the last reads.

choices.text: how long to leave it switched off before retrying
choices.why: Retrying is the expensive move here.

choices.text: whether to open it and free the head by hand
choices.why: That ends the possibility of recovery.

prompt: Nothing you have tried has changed anything at all. What does that suggest?

choices.text: the chain is being cut in the wrong place
choices.why: Rather than that the fault is mysterious.

choices.text: two separate faults are present at once
choices.why: Possible, and it is not the first reading.

choices.text: the fault is intermittent and has not appeared
choices.why: Then something would have changed once.

choices.text: the machine is beyond economical repair
choices.why: Nothing here supports that yet.

prompt: Match each symptom to what it means you should do.

pairs.left: the trackpad has risen and will not click
one file takes thirty seconds to open
it is slow only after half an hour
one key on the laptop is dead

prompt: Which symptom in this lesson is about the room rather than the machine?

choices.text: a battery that has swollen inside its case
choices.why: The only item here that is a safety matter.

choices.text: a hard disk that has started to click
choices.why: Urgent for the data, and not dangerous.

choices.text: a port that has to be held at an angle
choices.why: Mechanical, and it can wait a week.

choices.text: a power supply that restarts under load
choices.why: A fault, and not a hazard.

prompt: A machine crashes in three different programs and is not slow or noisy. What first?

choices.text: a full surface scan of the disk
choices.why: A disk gives itself away differently.

choices.text: a reinstall of the operating system
choices.why: The largest change available, and untested.

choices.text: a memory test from a stick, left to run
choices.why: Wandering crashes with no other signature.

choices.text: a clean-out of the dust and vents
choices.why: Heat makes it slow before it crashes.

prompt: Which of these is NOT a hardware fault at all?

choices.text: a keyboard producing the wrong characters entirely
choices.why: That is the layout setting, met earlier in this course.

choices.text: a keyboard that works only when pressed hard
choices.why: Wear under the keys.

choices.text: a keyboard where four keys next to each other are dead
choices.why: A spill.

choices.text: a keyboard that repeats one character all on its own
choices.why: A key not releasing, mechanically.

prompt: What single sentence is this lesson for?

choices.text: most hardware faults are really software faults
choices.why: The lesson argues the reverse.

choices.text: a failing machine should be replaced rather than fixed
choices.why: Often, and it is a separate calculation.

choices.text: any fault can be found with enough patience
choices.why: Some cannot, and stopping is part of the method.

choices.text: a failing machine is not one to keep using meanwhile
choices.why: Copy the files; everything after that is money.

prompt: Before testing a disk you suspect, ___ the files somewhere else.
